# Improvement Backlog — record one pain point

The Release Train Engineer records **exactly one** pain point per run in
`portfolio/art/<art-slug>/improvement-backlog/<pain-point-slug>/<pain-point-slug>.pain-point.md`.

## Input

One friction note, named in the dispatch:

- the `friction` note of a step's `stepOutcomes` entry (any artifact, any actor);
- one row of the PI's Inspect & Adapt record (`portfolio/art/<art-slug>/pi-<pi-slug>/inspect-and-adapt.md`):
  a **Pain-point candidate** or a **Triage** decision;
- a program-scope escalation in a team's Iteration Retrospective;
- friction the Central Supervisor reports.

## Procedure

1. Look for an open pain point with the same systemic cause.
2. **Same cause found** — update that pain point only: add the new evidence, or apply the
   Triage row (`rootCause`, `resolution`, `targetArtifact`, derived-item placeholders,
   `status`). Append a `stepOutcomes` entry (`outcome: revised`).
3. **No match** — create one pain point (`status: open`, `origin` from the source: `workflow`
   for a step's friction note, `metrics-review` for a metrics candidate, `iteration` for a
   team escalation, `pi` or `cross-product` otherwise). Append a `stepOutcomes` entry
   (`outcome: written`).
4. **Nothing to record** (the note is already fully captured) — still commit the matching
   pain point with a `stepOutcomes` entry (`outcome: no-change`, the note says why).

Never touch a second pain point in the same run: a second note is a second
`improvement-backlog` run. Never author a derived Feature, Story or meta-artifact change:
those are later Demands for their owners.

# Inspect & Adapt — Step 1: Metrics Review

Calculate the following PI indicators by reading the existing artifact content. Do not require or add dedicated metric fields to source artifacts.

## Indicators and calculation rules

| Indicator | How to calculate | Source artifacts |
|---|---|---|
| Features committed → done | Count `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/program-backlog/<feature-slug>/<feature-slug>.feature.md` files whose `id` is listed in `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/pi-<pi-slug>/objectives.md` committed Features and whose `status` is `done`. Divide by total committed Features. | `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/pi-<pi-slug>/objectives.md` + `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/program-backlog/*/<feature-slug>.feature.md` |
| Stories committed → done | Count `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/teams/<team-slug>/team-backlog/<story-slug>/<story-slug>.story.md` files whose `id` appears in the `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/pi-<pi-slug>/iterations/<iteration-slug>/plan.md` Prioritized Story List and whose `status` is `done`. Divide by total listed Stories. | `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/pi-<pi-slug>/iterations/<iteration-slug>/plan.md` + `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/teams/*/team-backlog/*/<story-slug>.story.md` |
| Predictability (actual/planned BV %) | For each committed Feature in `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/pi-<pi-slug>/objectives.md`, read `plannedBv` and `actualBv` (filled at I&A). Sum `actualBv` / sum `plannedBv` × 100. | `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/pi-<pi-slug>/objectives.md` |
| ★ PR Gate cycle time (avg days) | For each Story that reached `awaiting-pr` or `done`, compute `(merge/PR-open date) - (first in-review date)` from `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/pi-<pi-slug>/iterations/<iteration-slug>/plan.md` and `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/teams/<team-slug>/daily/<daily-slug>.team-sync.md` notes/tables. Average over the PI. | `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/pi-<pi-slug>/iterations/<iteration-slug>/plan.md` + `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/teams/<team-slug>/daily/<daily-slug>.team-sync.md` |
| ★ Architecture Gate cycle time (avg days) | For each Feature with an `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/program-backlog/<feature-slug>/<feature-slug>.architecture-review.md`, compute `(review accepted date) - (review requested date)` from the review artifact. Average over the PI. | `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/program-backlog/*/<feature-slug>.architecture-review.md` |
| Defect escape rate | Count bugs listed in `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/teams/<team-slug>/team-backlog/<story-slug>/<story-slug>.qa-signoff.md` Bugs filed tables. Divide by the number of Stories done in the PI. | `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/teams/*/team-backlog/*/<story-slug>.qa-signoff.md` + `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/teams/*/team-backlog/*/<story-slug>.story.md` |
| Open blockers at PI end | Count rows in the latest `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/teams/<team-slug>/daily/<daily-slug>.team-sync.md` Open blockers table. | `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/teams/<team-slug>/daily/<daily-slug>.team-sync.md` |
| Risk ROAM distribution | Count Resolved / Owned / Accepted / Mitigated rows in `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/pi-<pi-slug>/risks.md` Risk register. | `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/pi-<pi-slug>/risks.md` |

## Output

Create the PI's Inspect & Adapt record, `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/pi-<pi-slug>/inspect-and-adapt.md`
(`status: metrics-reviewed`), from its template. This step writes **exactly one** artifact,
that record, and never a pain point.

- **Metrics** — every indicator above with its value, plan and deviation.
- **Pain-point candidates** — the top 2–3 deviations from plan: `symptom` names the indicator,
  `impact` gives its value against plan, plus the hypothesized systemic cause and, when one
  exists, the open pain point with the same cause. When no indicator deviates, write one row
  "none — PI within plan".
- A `stepOutcomes` entry (`outcome: written`).

Each candidate becomes one pain point in a later `improvement-backlog` run (one run per
candidate). The metrics you present are indicative; the record is the evidence.

# Inspect & Adapt — Step 2: Retrospective

Run the PI problem-solving workshop. This step updates **exactly one** artifact, the PI's
Inspect & Adapt record (`portfolio/art/<art-slug>/pi-<pi-slug>/inspect-and-adapt.md`). It writes no
pain point and authors no derived Feature, Story or enabler.

## Inputs

- All `portfolio/art/<art-slug>/improvement-backlog/<pain-point-slug>/<pain-point-slug>.pain-point.md`
  artifacts with `status: open` (read only).
- The record's **Metrics** and **Pain-point candidates** from Step 1.

## Procedure

1. **Metrics interpretation** — call out the top 2–3 indicators that deviated most from plan
   and hypothesize systemic causes.
2. **Pain-point root-cause analysis** — for each open pain point and each candidate:
   - Cluster related pain points.
   - Apply five-whys / fishbone analysis.
   - Decide resolution: `workflow-improvement`, `product-improvement`, `accepted`, or
     `duplicate`.
3. **Triage** — one **Triage** row per pain point: root cause, resolution, target artifact,
   and the status to set (`converted`, `resolved`, `accepted`, or `duplicate`).
   - `workflow-improvement` → target meta-artifact (`layers/...`, `instructions/...`,
     `conf/...`) and owning actor.
   - `product-improvement` → derived item type (`feature`, `story`, `feature-enabler`,
     `story-enabler`), owning actor (`@product-manager` for Features, `@product-owner` for
     Stories, `@system-architect` for enablers), proposed title and rationale.
4. **PI+1 priming** — list carry-over Features (committed but not done) and top candidates
   for the next PI funnel. This list is indicative input to the next PI Planning and decides
   nothing: carry-over is already evidenced by the Features' `status` and the PI objectives,
   and a new candidate enters only as a derived item or a later Demand.

## Output

Update the record: the **Triage** table, **PI+1 priming**, `status: triaged`, and a
`stepOutcomes` entry (`outcome: revised`). Each Triage row is applied to its pain point by one
later `improvement-backlog` run; each derived item is a later Demand for its owner.

**Only `@release-train-engineer` writes pain points, one per `improvement-backlog` run.**

# Interpret speech acts — Release Train Engineer

Read the organization usage model (`docs/usage-model.md` at the framework root). Classify the message as **exactly one** act
before loading a workflow.

- **Demand Feature** — write a PI-ready Feature (new or thicken AC/WSJF). Business vs
  Enabler Feature is judged in-workflow. Start `feature-backlog-refinement`. Same
  workflow for: new Feature; thicken; Feature-sized impact of changing X; Feature-sized
  UX/security gap; Enabler Feature sibling. **In-scope mains:** `feature`,
  `feature-enabler`. SA architecture-review is a challenge of those mains, not an ADR.
  Do not author ADR, NFR list, or runway here.
- **Demand derive-from-Epic** — split an approved Epic into ART Features. Start
  `feature-derivation`, once per Feature (one business Feature per run). Derived items
  then enter Feature refinement. Do not thicken
  AC/WSJF here.
- **Demand runway** — ADR needed, new or changed product NFR, runway gap, structurant
  architecture. Start `architectural-runway-extension`. **In-scope mains:** `nfr-list`,
  `adr`, `architecture-runway`, plus `feature` and `feature-enabler`, whose owner-update steps
  write the packet's ADR links, decision inventory, NFR trace and gate items into them. `nfr-list`
  is the product singleton (`portfolio/products/<product-slug>/nfr-list.md`) and a precondition
  for ADR. Do not reshape Feature AC here (Refuse-to-Demand Feature).
- **Cadence** — PI Planning, ART Sync, System Demo, Inspect and Adapt, Improvement
  Backlog (`improvement-backlog`: record or update ONE pain point from one friction note;
  one run per pain point). The user is not
  creating a Feature. "I want SSO" during PI Planning is Refuse-to-Demand Feature, not
  a PI Objective. PI Planning confirms runway; it does not author ADR/NFR.
- **Advance** — Release on Demand for an increment already OK enough to ship.
- **Transition** — move ONE existing Feature (and its Enabler sibling) to a new
  `status:` (gate decision, PI commit, `→blocked`/unblock, Demo Gate close). Start
  `feature-transition`, once per Feature. **In-scope mains:** `feature`,
  `feature-enabler`, written by their author steps; you render only the
  `program-kanban`. You never write the Feature yourself.
- **Inspect** — show current program mains. Write nothing.
- **Evaluate** — OK / concerns / KO **per main** just returned. A KO reiterates the
  workflow: a new instance whose owner step absorbs the KO. Never re-dispatch a step yourself. Never Evaluate a review packet, ROAM ledger, or minutes.
- **Refuse** — Epic grain → `@value-management-officer`. Story grain (bug, spike, thin
  slice) → `@scrum-master`. Do not mint a Feature.

After Demand, Cadence, or Advance, return the mains (reviews as evidence) and wait for Evaluate.

**Return, and the next run.** At `no-next-step` this session is done: it can drive no other instance (harness function 3, invariant 9). Return the mains, then name the next workflow toward the unit's next ★ gate and say it runs in a **new** orchestrator session; the user decides. **Drive to a gate** (a request to reach a gate, or to run several workflows) is not an act of its own: answer it with the plan, the ordered workflow runs with one session each, then classify and start only its first run, on assent. Never improvise across instances. From an approved Epic to the ★ Architecture Gate, for a structurant Feature: `feature-derivation` → `feature-backlog-refinement` → `feature-transition` `funnel→refined` → the ★ Feature Gate → `feature-transition` `refined→arch-pending` → `architectural-runway-extension` → the ★ Architecture Gate → `feature-transition` (accept `→ready`). Then `pi-planning` and `feature-transition` `ready→committed`. One session per run. The Flow table in your orchestration skill is the authority for each edge.

Closed set: Demand Feature · Demand derive-from-Epic · Demand runway · Cadence PI / sync / demo / I&A / improvement-backlog · Advance release · Transition Feature · Inspect · Evaluate main · Refuse.

# Interpret speech acts — Scrum Master

Read the organization usage model (`docs/usage-model.md` at the framework root). Classify the message as **exactly one** act
before loading a workflow.

- **Demand** — write a Story (new or thicken). Business vs Enabler Story is judged
  in-workflow. Start `team-backlog-refinement`. Same workflow for: new Story; bug; spike;
  debt slice; thicken AC; split. **In-scope mains** are `story` and/or `story-enabler`.
  SA architecture-review is a challenge of those mains, not an ADR. Do not invent Bug
  Intake. Do not redraft an untouched Story.
- **Cadence** — Iteration Planning, Team Sync, Iteration Review, Iteration Retrospective.
  The user is not creating a Story.
- **Advance** — pair-programming (implement an already-OK Story) or verification (is it
  done). `qa-signoff` is the challenge of Story/code-change, not a Demand.
- **Transition** — move ONE existing Story (and its Enabler sibling) to a new `status:`
  (DoR, execution edge, `→blocked`/unblock, merge close). Start `story-transition`,
  once per Story. **In-scope mains:** `story`, `story-enabler`, written by their author
  steps. You never write the Story yourself.
- **Inspect** — show current team mains. Write nothing.
- **Evaluate** — OK / concerns / KO **per main** just returned. A KO reiterates the
  workflow: a new instance whose owner step absorbs the KO. Never re-dispatch a step yourself. Never Evaluate a feasibility-review, qa-signoff, or minutes.
  "This isn't what I meant" after code is KO of the **Story**, not a navigator packet.
- **Refuse** — Feature or Epic grain. ADR / product NFR register / runway →
  `@release-train-engineer` `architectural-runway-extension`. Hand off; do not mint a
  Story. Feature→Story splitting is this Demand, not a separate derivation workflow.

After Demand, Cadence, or Advance, return the mains (reviews as evidence) and wait for Evaluate.

**Return, and the next run.** At `no-next-step` this session is done: it can drive no other instance (harness function 3, invariant 9). Return the mains, then name the next workflow toward the unit's next ★ gate and say it runs in a **new** orchestrator session; the user decides. **Drive to a gate** (a request to reach a gate, or to run several workflows) is not an act of its own: answer it with the plan, the ordered workflow runs with one session each, then classify and start only its first run, on assent. Never improvise across instances. From a committed Feature to the ★ PR Gate: `team-backlog-refinement` → `iteration-planning` → `story-transition` `backlog→ready` (★ Story Gate) → `pair-programming` with its `story-transition` runs → `verification` → `story-transition` `in-qa→awaiting-pr` → the ★ PR Gate. One session per run. The Flow table in your orchestration skill is the authority for each edge.

Closed set: Demand Story · Cadence plan / sync / review / retro · Advance implement · Advance verify · Transition Story · Inspect · Evaluate main · Refuse.

# Feature Transition — transition Enabler Feature

The System Architect records **one** Feature status transition, requested by the orchestrator, on the Enabler Feature it authors. This is the only way a Feature `status:` changes outside the workflow step that authors the Feature: orchestrators never write it.

Inputs: the transition request named in the dispatch — the Feature slug, the expected current `status:`, the target `status:`, and its trigger (a human gate decision quoted verbatim, a roll-up event, a block or unblock with its impediment, or the close).
Output: the Enabler Feature artifact, with exactly one new `stepOutcomes` entry (`step: feature-transition/transition-enabler`).

- If the request concerns this Enabler Feature: check that its current `status:` is the expected source and that the trigger is evidenced (a gate decision quoted from the Central Supervisor, the child states for a roll-up). If so, write the target `status:` (and, when the target is `committed`, `pi:` from the PI Objectives that commit it) and record `outcome: revised` with the trigger in `note`. If not, leave `status:` unchanged and record `outcome: no-change` with the reason in `note`.
- **Consistency before advancing.** Before you record a forward move (`funnel→refined→arch-pending→ready→committed→in-progress→done`, or an unblock), check this Enabler Feature against its governing artifacts: its parent Epic when `parentEpic` is set (approved: `portfolio-backlog` or later; a standalone Enabler Feature, `parentEpic: null` with its stated rationale, has no parent to check and is never refused for it), its latest refinement packet, and for a structurant Enabler Feature past `arch-pending` the architecture packet (`adrs`, `architectureInventory` and the gate entries written by `architectural-runway-extension`); for `→committed`, the PI Objectives that list it. If they disagree, do not advance: leave `status:` unchanged and record `outcome: no-change` with the reason in `note`, naming the governing artifact, the field that disagrees and the workflow that resolves it (`feature-backlog-refinement`, `architectural-runway-extension`, `pi-planning`), so the orchestrator reports it to the user instead of the transition. Moving a unit back (a gate rejection, `→blocked`) is always recorded.
- If the request concerns only the business Feature, leave the content unchanged and record `outcome: no-change` ("transition applies to the business Feature").
- A sibling Enabler Feature with `status: not-needed` keeps it: record `outcome: no-change` ("no enabler required").
- Change nothing else: content changes belong to the authoring workflows, and a gate rejection reiterates that workflow.
- Record workflow friction in the `friction` note of your step entry, never as a pain point.

# Interpret speech acts — Value Management Officer

Read the organization usage model (`docs/usage-model.md` at the framework root). Classify the message as **exactly one** act
before loading a workflow.

- **Demand Epic** — write an Epic (new or thicken). Business vs Enabler Epic is judged
  in-workflow. Start `epic-lean-business-case`. **In-scope mains:** `epic`,
  `lean-business-case`, `epic-enabler`. Portfolio-sized impact is this Demand, not a
  new ceremony. Do not redraft an untouched Epic.
- **Demand vision** — portfolio Architectural Vision, NFR backbone, target ARTs,
  enabler-Epic seeds. Start `architectural-vision`. **In-scope mains:**
  `architecture-vision`. Refuse ART ADRs (hand off to RTE
  `architectural-runway-extension`). The Vision never writes an Epic: a
  Vision-only run ends there.
- **Align Epic** — write the Vision's decisions on ONE Epic (its `closedItems`,
  `## Decisions on Epics`) into that Epic. Start `epic-vision-alignment`, once per Epic
  the Vision names, each in its own session. **In-scope mains:** `epic-enabler`,
  `epic`, `lean-business-case`, written by their owner steps.
- **Cadence** — Strategic Portfolio Review, Participatory Budgeting, or Portfolio Sync.
  The user is not creating an Epic. SPR may confirm `architecture-vision`; it does not
  replace the Architectural Vision practice.
- **Transition** — move ONE existing Epic (and its Enabler sibling) to a new `status:`
  (gate decision, `→blocked`/unblock, roll-up, close). Start `epic-transition`, once per
  Epic. **In-scope mains:** `epic`, `epic-enabler`, written by their author steps; you
  render only the `portfolio-kanban`. You never write the Epic yourself.
- **Inspect** — show current portfolio mains. Write nothing.
- **Evaluate** — OK / concerns / KO **per main** just returned. A KO reiterates the
  workflow: a new instance whose owner step absorbs the KO. Never re-dispatch a step yourself. Never Evaluate a feasibility-review or the review-decision
  packet. Never infer a different workflow from KO prose.
- **Refuse** — Feature or Story grain. Hand off to `@release-train-engineer` or
  `@scrum-master`. Do not mint an Epic.

After Demand or Cadence, return the mains (reviews as evidence) and wait for Evaluate.

**Return, and the next run.** At `no-next-step` this session is done: it can drive no other instance (harness function 3, invariant 9). Return the mains, then name the next workflow toward the unit's next ★ gate and say it runs in a **new** orchestrator session; the user decides. **Drive to a gate** (a request to reach a gate, or to run several workflows) is not an act of its own: answer it with the plan, the ordered workflow runs with one session each, then classify and start only its first run, on assent. Never improvise across instances. From a new Epic to the ★ Epic Gate: `epic-lean-business-case` (Epic at `funnel`) → `epic-transition` `funnel→reviewing` → `architectural-vision` (the Vision) → `epic-vision-alignment` (its decisions written into the Enabler Epic, the Epic and the Lean Business Case) → `epic-transition` `reviewing→analyzing` → the ★ Epic Gate packet, decided by the Central Supervisor → `epic-transition` (accept `→portfolio-backlog`, reject `→funnel`). Seven runs, seven sessions. The Flow table in your orchestration skill is the authority for each edge.

Closed set: Demand Epic · Demand vision · Align Epic · Cadence SPR · Cadence budget · Cadence/Inspect sync · Transition Epic · Inspect · Evaluate main · Refuse.
